_nota: Inglés de `glossary.json` (`core/i18n.py`): castellano exacto → inglés, valor entero por valor entero. El fichero castellano no se toca; las claves, los ids y las frases literales de una fuente no se traducen. Lo aplica `i18n.localized` al servir.

strings.Lo que es normal para cada tripulante, c: What is normal for each crew member, computed from their own readings (median and median absolute deviation) and not from a population table. On a long mission what is normal shifts, and an Earth table would give false alarms at first and blindness later.
strings.Cuánto se aparta una lectura de la línea: How far a reading departs from the crew member's personal baseline. It serves for the acute, what has changed today; slow drift is a matter for the trend.
strings.Un cambio sostenido a lo largo de días o: A sustained change over days or weeks, separated from noise: a straight line is fitted to the series, and its slope only counts if it is clear against its own standard error.
strings.La proporción de alertas que da el siste: The proportion of alerts the system raises in healthy people, with no deterioration. EMMA measures it with real human physiology recorded on Earth (the MMASH dataset); it is not a test of flight physiology.
strings.La proporción de deterioros que el siste: The proportion of deteriorations the system detects when they are injected onto that same real physiology. It is measured together with the false alarm rate: a system that is switched off gives no false alarms and detects nothing either.
strings.Lo que tarda la luz, y con ella una tran: What light, and with it a radio transmission, takes between Earth and the spacecraft: 1.3 seconds to the Moon at its average distance and 3 to 22 minutes to Mars, depending on where the two planets are. With that delay Earth cannot answer at once, and EMMA scales risk with it.
strings.Una erupción gigante en la superficie de: A giant eruption on the surface of the Sun that sends energy into space in the form of X-rays, gamma rays and streams of protons and electrons. It can affect astronauts and their equipment even when they are far from the Sun.
strings.cuerpo de la página, sobre el Sol como f: body of the page, on the Sun as a source of radiation
strings.Las cinco categorías con que el Human Re: The five categories into which NASA's Human Research Program groups the hazards of human spaceflight: radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity (and its absence) and closed or hostile environments. RIDGE is formed by their initials in English; each EMMA risk domain carries its own.
strings.El registro por el que pasa toda observa: The record every observation passes through before it is stored: each entry is signed and chained to the previous one by its hash, so that a reading that is changed, deleted or cut off at the end is detected when the chain is verified.
strings.Un interruptor firmado que corta toda sa: A signed switch that cuts off every EMMA connection out to the internet. Anyone can turn it on with a reason and only a person lifts it; vital signs, the analysis and alerts keep working.
strings.Un valor que sale directamente de un sen: A value that comes directly from a sensor, from a test or from what the crew member notes down.
strings.Un valor estimado por un modelo a partir: A value estimated by a model from other measurements: no sensor read it.
strings.Un valor proyectado hacia el futuro, por: A value projected into the future, for example the continuation of a trend. It has not happened yet.
strings.Lo que hace EMMA: informa y propone, y l: What EMMA does: it informs and proposes, and the decision belongs to the crew and the medical team. It does not give medical orders or replace clinical judgment; that is why its texts pass through a language filter.
